summary.headline: RITES ends FY26 with record INR 9,416 crore order book; export income recovers to ~INR 300 crore, but management says FY27 profit records are unlikely.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 was in line with its roadmap, targeting double-digit growth with margins held. Q4 execution was about INR 750+ crore and the order book reached an all-time high of INR 9,416 crore on 31 March 2026, with over 50% of it 12-18 months old. Export income recovered to about INR 300 crore after nearly two years of decline, with a balance export order of about INR 1,750 crore led by 200 Bangladesh coaches. Management guided that revenue may hit an all-time high in FY27, but PAT and EBITDA records are not expected until at least two to three years out because of lower-margin turnkey mix.

financial_highlights.change: First increase after nearly two years

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Consultancy revenue of INR 1,185 crore rose 6% YoY across 13 verticals, with 700+ live consultancy orders. Quality assurance revenue grew 16% and is back to FY24 levels, with non-IR share now about 60%+.

segments.name: Turnkey
segments.commentary: Turnkey revenue fell by about INR 200 crore YoY. Turnkey order book of INR 4,580 crore is about two-thirds young (1-2 years), and management expects it to contribute more from FY27 at lower margins.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue of about INR 300 crore in FY26 came from 10 Mozambique locomotives. Bangladesh 200-coach order: first rake of 20 coaches due in about two months; prototypes approved.

segments.name: REMCL (leasing/power purchase consultancy)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 163 crore (up 16%), profit about INR 90 crore (up 19%), dividend about INR 42 crore. Growth limited to IR traffic volumes; new renewable and international consultancy orders being pursued.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for an all-time high revenue in FY27 but not an all-time high PAT or EBITDA; profit records may take two to three more years.
Profits will grow in FY27, though no number was given.
Management said PAT margin of 15% and EBITDA margin of 20% will not be breached, by monitoring high-margin orders.
Export execution in FY27 is expected to be well above INR 300 crore; a clearer figure is expected at end of Q1 FY27.
High dividend payout ratio to continue.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: 200 coaches in 10 rakes of 20; first rake targeted in about two months, with rakes at least three to four rakes apart in FY27 and production rate to step up after first delivery.
Converting spare Indian Railways diesel locomotives to Cape Gauge for African export: prototypes ready, first two units expected in coming months, with an order for about 30 in-service locomotives.
Electrification of Indian Railways is near 100%, so REMCL power-purchase consultancy growth is tied to traffic volumes.
demand_pricing: Order inflow run-rate is about one order a day and one export order a quarter; over 70% of fresh inflow is competitive, and 63% of the total order book is competitive.
Management said margins on new orders are much lower, so mix shift will pressure margins as new orders convert.

Turnkey fee economics: a 5% consultancy fee on a INR 100 crore project equals INR 5 crore; under turnkey the contract value is INR 105 crore but the scope and revenue are unchanged, so margins are lower.
Management sees no major impact from fuel or raw material costs because most contractor contracts have price variation clauses; travel costs are the main cost to watch.
Recent wins include an airport consultancy order and a Kandla shipbuilding cluster order; management sees no drop in strike rate despite budget capex concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management optimistic on disruptive growth given geopolitical headwinds, and can margins be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book has risen over the last 7-8 quarters, with over 50% of it 12-18 months old and set to convert in FY27. Margins on new orders are lower, so margins will dilute as they convert, but PAT of 15% and EBITDA of 20% will be defended.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise and will they stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses came from logistics for moving the 10 Mozambique locomotives (six moved in Q4) and warranty provisions tied to export execution. FY27 will see a slight increase, partly offset by lower logistics costs on rail-moved Bangladesh coaches.

qa_highlights.question: How much export revenue can come in FY27 from the INR 1,700+ crore balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aiming well above INR 300 crore but cannot give a firm number yet; a clearer figure is expected at end of Q1 FY27 once the first rake moves.

qa_highlights.question: When will turnkey revenue recover to last year's level?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnkey revenue was about INR 200 crore lower YoY. Turnkey order book of INR 4,580 crore is about two-thirds young, and management expects it to reach last year's turnkey revenue levels as IIT/IIM building and rail siding projects start generating revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government capex cut delay railway contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major impact on consultancy from fresh orders or milestone progress, citing recent wins across railways, PSUs, ports, highways and airports.

risks_watch: Margin dilution as competitive and turnkey orders (63% of order book competitive) convert to revenue; PAT and EBITDA margin floors of 15% and 20%.
Bangladesh export timeline: first rake due in about two months, and rake pace depends on production ramp-up.
Turnkey revenue still below last year and dependent on young projects reaching milestones.
Possible capex slowdown from government fiscal pressures, though management sees no impact so far.
Rising travel and logistics costs on international projects and export movements.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, revenue and FY27 growth, but explicitly cautious on profit, saying PAT and EBITDA records are unlikely this year. Management was specific on the Bangladesh and turnkey timelines but gave no firm export or profit numbers.
key_quotes: So, the order book currently of INR 9,400 crore, a substantial portion, more than 50% of it, is very young, which is about, as I said, 12 to 18 months old.
But this is for sure, it will be much higher than INR 300 crore.
So, the margins across our streams, the margins on the new orders are much lower.
We are not a construction company. We are a project management consultancy company.

Conversion of spare Indian Railways diesel locomotives to Cape Gauge for African export (first two units in coming months, ~30 in-service locomotives order)

growth.why: Management aims for an all-time high revenue in FY27 and says profits will grow (no number), with export execution well above INR 300 crore; backing is a record INR 9,416 crore order book, a Bangladesh 200-coach order and Cape Gauge locomotive conversions, but no FY27 revenue figure was given and PAT/EBITDA records are not expected for 2-3 years due to lower-margin turnkey mix.
